gaps.sentence: My laptop ___ (service) next week, so back up your files beforehand.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' takes the future passive: will be + serviced (is being serviced is also a valid arrangement).

gaps.sentence: Your contract will ___ for a further twelve months.
gaps.explanation: After 'will', passive = be + past participle: will be renewed.

gaps.sentence: The finalists ___ (interview) live on air as we speak.
gaps.explanation: 'As we speak' demands the present continuous passive: are being + interviewed.

gaps.sentence: Did you have the brakes ___ (check) before the long drive?
gaps.hint: question form of have something done
gaps.explanation: Causative question: Did you have + the brakes + checked? A mechanic did the checking.

gaps.sentence: The matter ___ at this very moment, so no comment yet.
gaps.explanation: Look into (investigate) passivises with the particle kept: is being looked into.

gaps.sentence: The manuscript is too fragile ___ (handle) without gloves.
gaps.explanation: Passive to-infinitive: to be + past participle. The manuscript receives the handling.

gaps.sentence: There's still a lot of paperwork ___ (complete) before we can close the account.
gaps.explanation: Noun + passive to-infinitive (paperwork to be completed) — the paperwork receives the action.

gaps.sentence: She hates ___ (interrupt) when she's deep in work.
gaps.explanation: Passive gerund: being + past participle, after verbs like hate, like, avoid.
